visual_elements.description: 3D coordinate system with axes labeled y (vertical, red), x1 (lower left, red), x2 (right, red). A yellow tilted plane (parallelogram) labeled 'W' in black with underline. On the plane: four data points marked as small dots (blue and orange/brown) with axis tick labels '1' and '2' on x1 and x2 axes. A red arrow points into the plane with label '-ve ( < 0 )' in red above the plane, and '+ve ( > 0 )' in blue below-left of the plane, indicating the two half-spaces.

Upper right box: rows 'x1 ⇒' and 'x2 ⇒' in blue, followed by four column vectors X1=(1,1), X2=(2,2), X3=(2,1), X4=(1,2); beneath each, class labels y1=C1 (red), y2=C2 (blue), y3=C1 (red), y4=C2 (blue). Below: 'Classify' in green italic, X=(7,3) in blue, then 'y = C1 or C2 ???' with C1 red, C2 blue.

Lower right green box: header 'Required to obtain W that satisfies' with W in red underlined. Matrix equation: rows labeled x1 ⇒, x2 ⇒, x3 ⇒, x4 ⇒ (blue); 4x3 matrix with rows (1 1 1), (1 2 2), (1 2 1), (1 1 2) in red; multiplied by vector W (red, in parentheses); equals a column vector of inequalities: > 0, < 0, > 0, < 0 (red).
Footer beige/tan box with bold text: How to deal “Mathematically” with “<” and “>” ??? — the word 'Mathematically' in red, rest in black.

recreation_brief: 1. White background slide. 2. Top center: bold title 'Classification ' in blue + 'Example' in red. 3. Top-right: yellow circle with '32'. 4. Left: draw a red-bordered rectangle (~40% width, most of height); inside draw 3D axes (y up, x1 lower-left, x2 right) in red with arrowheads; add a yellow rotated parallelogram plane labeled 'W' (underlined); place 4 small dots on it with tick labels 1,2 on axes; add red arrow with red text '-ve ( < 0 )' above plane and blue text '+ve ( > 0 )' below-left. 5. Upper right: gray-bordered box; inside put blue 'x1 ⇒' / 'x2 ⇒' row labels, then four column vectors X1=(1;1), X2=(2;2), X3=(2;1), X4=(1;2); below them labels y1=C1 (red), y2=C2 (blue), y3=C1 (red), y4=C2 (blue); then green italic 'Classify' and blue X=(7;3); then 'y = C1 or C2 ???' with C1 red, C2 blue. 6. Lower right: light green box; header 'Required to obtain W that satisfies' with W red underlined; below, rows x1..x4 ⇒ (blue) with red matrix rows (1 1 1),(1 2 2),(1 2 1),(1 1 2), times red vector W, equals column (>0, <0, >0, <0) in red. 7. Bottom: beige box with bold text 'How to deal “Mathematically” with “<” and “>” ???' with 'Mathematically' in red.
